user.title: Grid Lens Setup
user.description:
Grid Lens compares your real metered electricity usage against every plan on your network, so you can see what you'd pay on each one.

Setup is three short screens.

data_description.state: Used to look up the plans and network tariffs that apply to you.
data_description.gridlens_email: Creates your free Grid Lens account. We don't send marketing email.

distributor.title: Select Your Network Distributor
distributor.description: More than one network in your state has plan data. Choose the distributor that operates the poles and wires at your address — it's printed on your electricity bill, and it determines which plans and network tariffs apply to you.

sensors.title: Energy Sensors
sensors.description:
{discovered}

Grid import and export sensors must measure cumulative energy (kWh/MWh) with state_class: total_increasing — not instantaneous power (W/kW).

data_description.energy_sensor: Cumulative kWh/MWh imported from the grid. Must have state_class: total_increasing.
data_description.solar_sensor: Cumulative kWh/MWh generated by your solar panels.
data_description.grid_export_sensor: Cumulative kWh/MWh exported to the grid.
data_description.grid_power_sensor: A live power sensor reading your home's net grid flow, in watts. Positive = importing from the grid, negative = exporting. Used by the Greedy Consumption feature to detect real export surplus. Optional.
data_description.import_price_sensor: Current import price in $/kWh from your retailer (e.g. sensor.flow_power_nsw1_import_price, sensor.amber_nsw1_general_price). Used to calculate your actual current-plan cost.
data_description.export_price_sensor: Current feed-in/export price in $/kWh from your retailer (e.g. sensor.flow_power_nsw1_export_price, sensor.amber_nsw1_feed_in_price).

battery.title: Battery Configuration
battery.description:
If you have a home battery, configure it here.

• Your current plan cost uses **actual** battery behaviour from your sensors.
• Alternative plans show costs with **optimally** scheduled battery usage so you can see the true potential saving.

Efficiency and charge limits use sensible defaults — adjust them later under **Configure** if you need to.

data_description.battery_capacity: Total usable capacity in kWh (e.g. Sigenergy 10 kWh)
data_description.battery_min_soc: Reserve charge level to keep for backup (%)
data_description.battery_max_soc: Maximum charge level for battery health (%)
data_description.battery_soc_sensor: Sensor reporting current battery charge as a percentage (0–100).
data_description.battery_charge_power_sensor: Sensor for battery charging power. Use a signed sensor (positive = charging, negative = discharging) and leave Discharge blank — or supply two separate unipolar sensors (one for each direction).
data_description.battery_discharge_power_sensor: Discharge power sensor if separate from the charge sensor. Leave blank if your charge sensor is signed (negative when discharging).

devices.title: Deferrable Loads
devices.description:
These appliances were found in your Energy Dashboard. Select any that can be **rescheduled to cheaper hours** — the optimizer will find the best time to run them under each plan.

Typical deferrable loads: EV charger, pool pump, dishwasher, washing machine, water heater.

device_power.title: Deferrable Load Power Limits
device_power.description:
For each appliance, enter its maximum rated power — this caps how much the optimizer can assign it in any hour.

Optionally pick a **control entity** (a `switch.*` or `climate.*` entity) so Grid Lens can run that load at the cheapest times. Each one gets its own master switch, off until you enable it. Leave blank to have Grid Lens forecast around the device without controlling it.

Everything else — allowed run hours, controlled-load wiring, and modulating (variable-current) charger control — is set after setup: run hours on the **Deferrable Loads** dashboard card, the rest under **Configure**.

current_plan.title: Your Current Plan
current_plan.description:
Select the electricity plan you are currently on.

This creates your **free Grid Lens account**, which compares your current plan against itself so you can see your cost breakdown.

[Upgrade at gridlens.au/pricing](https://gridlens.au/pricing) to compare against all available plans on your network and find out if you could be paying less.

data.has_demand_tariff: My network bills a demand charge

data_description.has_demand_tariff: Tick this if your *current* network bills a demand (peak kW) charge — it's set by your distributor based on your meter, so check your bill for a 'demand' line in $/kW. This only affects plans priced against your network's demand charge. A plan whose own tariff is a demand tariff (e.g. Amber's demand-tariff variant) always includes it. When a demand charge applies, the battery optimiser also shaves your peak to reduce it.
data_description.vpp_program: If you're enrolled in a retailer VPP credit program on top of your plan (e.g. AGL Bring Your Own Battery), select it here. This is independent of your plan choice — switching plans with the same retailer won't affect it. Leave as 'None / not enrolled' if you're not in one.
data_description.network_tariff_codes: Some plans only apply to a specific network tariff (found on your bill, e.g. 'EA116'). Enter your code(s), comma-separated, to hide plans that don't match. Leave blank if you don't know it — nothing is filtered until you set this, and it's never sent to Grid Lens.

manual_key.title: This Installation Already Has a Key
manual_key.description:
This Home Assistant installation is already registered with Grid Lens under **{email}**, so a new key can't be issued for it.

This is normal if you've removed and re-added the integration. Paste the key you saved when you first set it up.

We only ever store a hashed copy of your key, so we can't show it to you again. If you've lost it, contact support@gridlens.au from your registered email address and we'll issue a replacement.

error.wrong_unit_power: This sensor measures power (W/kW), not energy. You need a cumulative energy sensor (kWh/MWh).
error.wrong_unit: Wrong unit of measurement — must be kWh or MWh.
error.wrong_state_class: This sensor does not have state_class: total_increasing. It may not be a cumulative energy sensor.
error.invalid_capacity: Battery capacity must be greater than 0 kWh.
error.invalid_hours: Invalid availability hours — use 'all' or ranges like '18-08' or '0-6,12-14'.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the GridLens API. Check the API URL and your internet connection.
error.invalid_api_key: Invalid API key — check the key and try again.

abort.state_not_supported: Grid Lens doesn't have plan data for {state} yet, so it can't compare anything for you. Coverage is being added state by state — register at https://gridlens.au to be told when yours is ready.

controlled_load.title: Controlled Load
controlled_load.description: Does your meter have a Controlled Load circuit switched by your network distributor? This is a network/meter fact, not a retail plan setting.

data_description.has_controlled_load_1: Tick if your meter has a Controlled Load 1 (CL1) circuit — commonly used for hot water or a pool pump, switched on by your network at set times.
data_description.has_controlled_load_2: Tick if your meter has a Controlled Load 2 (CL2) circuit, a second switched register some networks offer.

data_description.solar_sensor: Cumulative kWh/MWh generated by your solar panels.

loads.title: Deferrable Loads
loads.description:
A deferrable load is an appliance whose run time can be moved to cheaper hours — a pool pump, hot water, an EV charger, a dishwasher.

Pick one to change it, or add another. Each load is set up on its own, and you are only asked what that load actually needs.

**Currently configured:**
{summary}

Run times are not set here — paint them on the Deferrable Loads dashboard card's weekly schedule. Every load is unrestricted (any hour) until you do.

data.action: What would you like to do?

load_kind.title: Add a Deferrable Load
load_kind.description: What Grid Lens can already see and do for this appliance decides everything else it needs to ask.

menu_options.load_add_monitored: It has an energy sensor — pick it from my Energy Dashboard
menu_options.load_add_estimated: No energy sensor, but I can switch it on and off from HA
menu_options.load_add_declared: No energy sensor and no way to control it — forecast only

load_add_monitored.title: Which Appliance?
load_add_monitored.description: These are the individual devices tracked on your Home Assistant Energy Dashboard. Appliances already configured as deferrable loads aren't listed.

load_detail_monitored.title: {name}
load_detail_monitored.description:
**{name}** is measured by an energy sensor, so Grid Lens knows what it actually uses.

Maximum power caps how much the optimizer can assign it in any half-hour — use the appliance's rated draw.

How Grid Lens controls it decides what's asked next: **forecast only** plans around it but never touches it; **on/off** needs a `switch.*` or `climate.*` entity; **modulating** is for a charger whose current or power can be ramped up and down rather than only switched.

data.control_style: How should Grid Lens control it?
data.has_soc: This device has its own battery (e.g. an EV)
data.on_controlled_load: This device is wired to a Controlled Load circuit

load_detail_declared.title: {name}
load_detail_declared.description:
**Grid Lens cannot switch a declared load on or off — it only forecasts around it.** This is the normal case for a genuine Controlled Load circuit, which is wired separately from whatever your inverter's CT clamp monitors and so usually has no sensor to point at.

Give it an estimated **average daily kWh** and Grid Lens will schedule that energy into the cheapest hours it's allowed to run.

Available hours accepts `all`, a range like `22-06`, or a comma-separated list like `9-15,22-24`.

data.name: Name
data.on_controlled_load: This device is wired to a Controlled Load circuit

load_detail_estimated.title: {name}
load_detail_estimated.description:
**Grid Lens can switch this load on and off**, it just can't measure it. Give it the entity to control and roughly what the appliance draws when running, and Grid Lens will schedule it like any other deferrable load.

Both a name and a control entity are required — a load with only one of them would be silently ignored.

Turn on **refine automatically** to have Grid Lens learn the real draw over time by watching your whole-house load when this device switches on. That needs a house load power sensor, set from the Deferrable Loads menu.

load_control.title: {name} — On/Off Control
load_control.description:
The `switch.*` or `climate.*` entity Grid Lens will turn on and off to run **{name}** at the best times.

Control starts disabled: each load gets its own master switch, off by default, that you turn on when you're ready to let Grid Lens actuate it.

The **"on" mode** below is only consulted for a `climate.*` entity that doesn't support turn on/off — most do, so leave it on Auto unless yours misbehaves.

load_modulating.title: {name} — Modulating Control
load_modulating.description:
A charging current or power setpoint lets Grid Lens ramp **{name}** continuously instead of just switching it — following your solar surplus as it changes rather than running flat out or not at all.

The setpoint is a `number.*` entity such as OCPP's `maximum_current`, Easee's `dynamic_charger_limit`, Wallbox's `maximum_charging_current`, or the equivalent on Zaptec, go-e, openEVSE, Tesla or a Sigenergy AC charger.

Unit, phase count and voltage default to auto-detected values that are right for almost every install. Minimum current defaults to the 6 A EV charging floor. A plug/connected sensor lets Grid Lens avoid commanding current into an empty socket.

Live solar-surplus tracking also needs the Grid Power sensor configured on the Energy Sensors step — without it this charger follows the optimizer's plan and never chases a passing cloud.

load_soc.title: {name} — State of Charge
load_soc.description:
**{name}** has its own battery, so Grid Lens can stop scheduling charge once it's nearly full instead of pushing past a limit you set on purpose.

Its state of charge is shown on the Power Flow card alongside the home battery's.

The charge ceiling and capacity work together: once the battery is within reach of the ceiling, the optimizer frees that energy for other loads or export. Capacity must be greater than zero for this to take effect.

load_cl.title: {name} — Controlled Load
load_cl.description:
Which Controlled Load register **{name}** is wired to.

Turn on **already counted in main reading** only if this load's energy is currently mixed into your main energy sensor — for example a general-circuit appliance you're considering moving to Controlled Load. Leave it off for a load already on a genuinely separate register, which is the normal case: your main sensor never saw it in the first place.

load_power.title: House Load Power Sensor
load_power.description:
A whole-house load power sensor lets Grid Lens refine estimated loads automatically: when an estimated load switches on, the step change in total house draw is what that appliance is actually using.

Only needed if you turned on **refine automatically** for an estimated load.

api_key.title: API Key & Connection
api_key.description:
Your API key unlocks every plan on your network so you can see which one actually suits you.

Leave unchanged to keep your current key, or paste a new one below.

Get a key at [gridlens.au/pricing](https://gridlens.au/pricing).
